newsitem.title: CHINA: China's grand old lady panda totters toward death.
newsitem.headline: China's grand old lady panda totters toward death.

text.p: Zookeepers in China's central city of Wuhan are struggling to keep the nation's oldest caged panda alive -- but are ready to build her a mausoleum when she finally departs for the great bamboo grove in the sky.
Panda Dudu was blind, unable to eat solids and fighting disease, the Xinhua news agency said on Friday.

At the grand old age of 35, porridge-sipping Dudu had already lived five years longer than the most venerable panda previously reported and had far exceeded the usual panda life expectancy of six to 20 years, the agency said.

"She lost her eyesight due to keratitis. And because she has lost most of her teeth, she hasn't eaten her favourite food -- bamboo leaves -- for eight years," it quoted Wuhan zoo keeper Chen Jun as saying.

The zoo was supplying intensive medical care for Dudu, who had mated once but never had children, but were prepared for the worst and planned to accord the aged panda an honour usually reserved for senior leaders, it said.
"Her owner is even ready to build a mausoleum and a monument," it said but gave no details.
She celebrated her 35th birthday with a special bowl of milk last month.
